title: Conditional Compilation
concept: Conditional compilation selectively includes or excludes code depending on the build environment

steps.title: Including stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
**`#include <stdio.h>`** -- Includes the header for `printf`.

In this lesson we learn **Conditional Compilation**.

steps.title: Defining the compilation switch
steps.explanation: **`#define DEBUG_MODE 1`** -- A macro that acts as a **switch** for the `#ifdef` and `#if` directives below, determining which code to include. Changing this value or removing the line entirely excludes debug code from compilation.

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation: **`int main() {`** -- The program entry point. At this point, the preprocessor has already completed header insertion, macro definitions, and code inclusion/removal based on `#ifdef`/`#if` conditions.

steps.title: First output
steps.explanation: **`printf("Program Start\n");`** -- This is not inside any `#ifdef` or `#if` block, so it is **always** compiled and executed regardless of conditions. `"Program Start"` is printed.

steps.title: Conditional compilation 1: #ifdef
steps.explanation: **`#ifdef DEBUG_MODE`** -- Checks whether `DEBUG_MODE` is **defined**. If it has been `#define`d with any value, the condition is true; if not defined, it is false.

steps.title: Debug code execution
steps.explanation: **`printf("[DEBUG] Variable x checking...\n");`** -- Since the `#ifdef` condition was true, the preprocessor kept this line, and it is compiled and executed. `"[DEBUG] Variable x checking..."` is printed.

steps.title: Conditional compilation 2: #if
steps.explanation: **`#if DEBUG_MODE == 0`** -- Unlike `#ifdef`, this **directly compares the macro's value**. `#ifdef` only checks existence, but `#if` evaluates the expression to determine true/false.

steps.title: Final output
steps.explanation:
**`printf("Program End\n");`** -- Outside any conditional block, so it always executes.

Analyzing the final output: `"Program Start"` -- unconditional, `"[DEBUG]..."` -- included because `#ifdef` was true, `"Release Mode"` -- excluded because `#if` was false.
steps.stdout:
Program Start
[DEBUG] Variable x checking...
Program End

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
**`return 0;`** -- The program terminates.

Practical uses of conditional compilation: separating debug/release builds (`#ifdef DEBUG`), platform-specific code (`#ifdef _WIN32`, `#ifdef __linux__`), and more.

quiz.question: What is the main reason for using Header Guards (#ifndef HEADER_H ...)?
options: Preventing duplicate header inclusion (avoiding redefinition errors)
quiz.explanation:
If the same header is included multiple times in a source file (directly or indirectly), structs or functions get redefined, causing compilation errors.
Header guards prevent this.

misconceptions.wrong: Code excluded by #ifdef is checked at runtime like an if statement.
misconceptions.correct:
There is no condition check at runtime at all.
During preprocessing, the code is either removed or kept -- one or the other.
misconceptions.why: This affects the actual executable file size.

keyTakeaway: With conditional compilation, a single source code can produce separate executables for debug, release, and different OS targets (Windows/Linux).
